item.text: I found the core failure: version normalization treats any one-token release as Amazon Linux 1, while the EOL map only knows through 2022. I’m checking the existing EOL test cases and Amazon detection path so the fix preserves legacy formats while recognizing newer release strings.

item.text: The normalizer now explicitly accepts supported release numbers, maps dotted `YYYY.MM` strings to Amazon Linux 1, and returns `unknown` for anything else. I’ve added EOL dates for the requested releases; I’m adding focused regression coverage, including the standard versus extended support boundary behavior already represented by `EOL`.

The focused `config` tests are still running (likely compiling the package and its dependencies); no failure output has appeared. Once they finish, I’ll record the result in the checkpoint and inspect the diff.
